purpose: give every developer a quick, repeatable way to build, run and test the system locally, matching production closely enough to trust the results
entry_criteria: The repository and its dependencies are known
A container or provisioning tool is chosen
procedure: Define the toolchain versions in a file that tools read, so everyone uses the same versions.
Provide a single command or short script to set up dependencies and start the system with its services.
Use synthetic or masked data, never raw production data or real credentials.
Keep configuration in environment files with an example file in the repository and secrets outside it.
Document the differences from production that matter and how to test them elsewhere.
Test the setup on a clean machine or container and record the time it takes.
acceptance_criteria: A newcomer is running within the stated time
No real secrets or production data are used

validation.command: docker compose up -d && docker compose ps   # example; use the project's start command

failure_modes.response: Pin versions and test on a clean machine
Make the script the source and test it in CI

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A single make target starts the app, database and queue in containers with pinned versions and synthetic data, and a clean laptop is ready in twelve minutes.
